title: When Did Oklahoma Join the SEC? The Sooners' 2024 Move
question: When did the Oklahoma Sooners officially join the SEC?
answer: Oklahoma officially became a member of the Southeastern Conference on July 1, 2024, joining alongside Texas and growing the SEC to 16 schools. The Sooners played their first SEC game on Sept. 21, 2024, against Tennessee in Norman.
summary: Oklahoma officially joined the SEC on July 1, 2024, alongside Texas, after leaving the Big 12 a year early. Here is the timeline and the first SEC game.
body: For Sooner fans, July 1, 2024, is a date to remember. That Monday, Oklahoma and Texas officially became members of the Southeastern Conference, closing the book on OU's 30 years in the Big 12 and turning the SEC into a 16-team league.

The move had been building for three years. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey has said both schools first approached him in the spring of 2021. SEC presidents voted unanimously to admit both schools, and the plan became public in July 2021. The original timeline pointed to 2025, when the Big 12's grant of media rights was set to expire.

That changed on Feb. 9, 2023, when the Big 12 and the departing schools announced a deal for Oklahoma and Texas to leave a year earlier than planned, with each school giving up a share of future Big 12 media money. With final approvals in place, the effective date became July 1, 2024. OU athletic director Joe Castiglione described the SEC as a natural fit for the Sooners.

On the field, the SEC welcome was tough. Oklahoma's first-ever SEC game came on Sept. 21, 2024, in Norman against Tennessee, coached by former Sooner national-title quarterback Josh Heupel. The Volunteers won 25-15. OU finished its first SEC season 6-7, then bounced back in 2025 with a 10-2 regular season and a College Football Playoff berth.
